scene: BNC package lying on a bright tiled floor, photographed from above at a slight angle
why: Physical QA failure. The guide was visible in only 19 of 1214 analysed frames (1.6%) on this exact scene, and the crop polygon locked onto an edge inside the package instead of its outer boundary. Every synthetic fixture used a clean object on a uniform background, which is why none of them reproduced it: here the floor carries many long, strong, straight grout lines at several angles, and they compete directly with the package's own edges in the Hough stage.

detectorInput.format: 8-bit binary PGM (P5) — the raw luma plane
detectorInput.normalization: none applied to the stored file; the detector performs its own local normalization
detectorInput.provenance: written by MainScanFixtureExporter from the exact LumaFrame handed to the detector

groundTruth.note: Normalized to the 240x180 fixture. Read off a 5x magnified grid render of frame 01; the scene is near-static across the three frames, so the same annotation applies to all with a slightly wider tolerance.

prohibited.note: Regions the polygon must NOT latch onto. These are the failure modes actually observed, not hypotheticals.
prohibited.fullFrame: must not fall back to image bounds while the package is plainly detectable
prohibited.floorGroutLines: the long tile seams crossing the frame must not supply any side
prohibited.packageInterior: the boundary between the package's red panel and its yellow bands must not be used in place of the outer edge
